title: Retry Behavior
content: DevFlow retries failed pipeline steps up to 3 times by default, with exponential backoff starting at 10 seconds. Retries are NOT idempotent-safe by default — if a step has side effects like sending a notification or writing to a database, it will re-run those side effects on every retry. To make a step safe to retry, wrap it with the `idempotent: true` flag in your devflow.yaml, which causes DevFlow to record a completion token and skip the step body if it already succeeded.

title: Pipeline Timeouts
content: Each pipeline step has a default timeout of 15 minutes. This can be overridden per-step using the `timeout` field (in seconds) in devflow.yaml. If a step exceeds its timeout, DevFlow marks it as failed and triggers the retry policy, not a hard pipeline failure, unless retries are also exhausted.

title: Secrets Management
content: Secrets are injected as environment variables at runtime and are never written to disk or logs. DevFlow automatically redacts any string matching a registered secret value from step output logs. Secrets must be registered in the DevFlow dashboard under Settings > Secrets before they can be referenced in devflow.yaml using the `${{ secrets.NAME }}` syntax.

title: Parallel Steps
content: Steps in the same `stage` block run in parallel by default. To force sequential execution within a stage, add `sequential: true` to the stage definition. Parallel steps that fail do not automatically cancel their sibling steps unless `fail_fast: true` is set at the pipeline level.

title: Caching
content: DevFlow caches dependencies (e.g. node_modules, pip packages) between runs using a hash of your lockfile as the cache key. Cache entries expire after 7 days of inactivity. If a build behaves unexpectedly after a dependency change, clearing the cache manually via `devflow cache clear` often resolves it, since stale caches are a common source of confusing build failures.

title: Webhook Triggers
content: Pipelines can be triggered by GitHub webhooks (push, pull_request, release) or by a manual API call to the /trigger endpoint. Webhook payloads are verified using HMAC-SHA256 against your configured webhook secret; DevFlow rejects any webhook with an invalid or missing signature.

title: Environment Promotion
content: DevFlow supports promoting a build artifact from staging to production without rebuilding, using `devflow promote <build_id> --to production`. This requires the artifact to still exist in the build cache, which is retained for 30 days. Promotions require manual approval by default, configurable under Settings > Environments.

title: Notification Channels
content: DevFlow can send pipeline status notifications to Slack, email, or a custom webhook. Notification rules are configured per-pipeline and can filter by status (success, failure, cancelled). By default only failure notifications are enabled to avoid notification fatigue on high-frequency pipelines.

title: Matrix Builds
content: Matrix builds let you run the same step across multiple parameter combinations, e.g. multiple Node versions or OS targets, defined using a `matrix` block. Each matrix combination runs as an independent parallel job, and a single failing combination does not fail the others unless `fail_fast: true` is set.

title: Rollback Behavior
content: If a deployment step fails after partially applying changes, DevFlow does not automatically roll back unless a `rollback` step is explicitly defined in devflow.yaml. Without a rollback step defined, a failed deployment can leave the environment in a partially updated state, which is a common source of production incidents.
